extracted.intended_audience: pharmaceutical and plant protection product patent holders, IP practitioners, and national intellectual property offices in the EU
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for obtaining Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPCs) in the EU for medicines and plant protection products, covering eligibility, filing procedure, term/limits, waivers and paediatric extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Supplementary Protection Certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary protection certificate: an intellectual property right for a specific product that acts as an extension of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides additional protection for specific patented pharmaceutical and plant protection products that have been approved for sale; designed to offset reduction in effective patent protection and encourage innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic patent protection requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any pharmaceutical or plant protection product may receive an SPC, where: it is protected by a national patent (the basic patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SPC is an extension of the rights conferred by the basic patent, so a valid national patent covering the product is a precondition for SPC eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing authorisation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any pharmaceutical or plant protection product may receive an SPC, where: it must have national or EU authorisation before it may be sold (marketing authorisation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marketing authorisation (national or EU) is required before an SPC can be granted; the date the authorisation is granted is relevant for application deadlines and overall protection calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No existing certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Any pharmaceutical or plant protection product may receive an SPC, where: it does not already have a certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SPC cannot be granted for a product that already benefits from an SPC; i.e., no duplicate SPCs for the same product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and when to file the SPC application
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPC application must be lodged with the relevant national industrial property office: within 6 months of the marketing authorisation being granted; or where the marketing authorisation is granted before the basic patent is granted, within 6 months of the date on which the patent is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict filing deadlines apply (6 months) and the application must be filed at the national IP office competent for the basic patent; the relevant trigger date depends on the sequencing of patent grant and marketing authorisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rights conferred by an SPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPC confers the same rights as those provided by the basic patent, apart from the limitations of the manufacturing waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPC holders generally enjoy the same exclusivity as under the basic patent, subject to statutory exceptions introduced by later legislation (notably the manufacturing waiver).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing waiver (Regulation (EU) 2019/933) exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Amending Regulation (EU) 2019/933 introduced a manufacturing waiver to the protection given by an SPC for pharmaceutical products that allows EU-based companies to manufacture a generic or similar version of an SPC-protected medicine during the term of the certificate: either for exporting to a non‑EU market; or for stockpiling during the final 6 months of an SPC, ahead of entry into the EU market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This waiver limits the exclusivity conferred by SPCs for pharmaceuticals by permitting certain manufacturing and export/stockpiling acts within the EU under the specified conditions; the waiver applies to SPCs for medicinal products as amended from 1 July 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPC start date and maximum term
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPC takes effect when the basic patent expires, and is valid for up to 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SPC does not run concurrently with the basic patent but begins at patent expiry; statutory maximum duration for an SPC is five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall protection cap (patent + SPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall protection a patent and an SPC can provide may not be more than 15 years from the granting of the first marketing authorisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calculating total effective exclusivity, the combined term of the basic patent and any SPC(s) is capped at 15 years measured from the date of the first marketing authorisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paediatric extension (6-month SPC extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPC may be extended once for 6 months for pharmaceutical products for children where a paediatric investigation plan has been prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the paediatric investigation plan (PIP) condition is met, a single 6‑month extension may be added to the SPC term, producing an overall maximum protection of 15.5 years from the first marketing authorisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory applicability and temporal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation (EC) No 1610/96 (SPC for plant protection products) has applied since 8 February 1997 (or since 2 January 1998 in countries whose national law did not cover patentability of plant protection products). Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 (SPC for medicinal products) has applied since 6 July 2009. Amending Regulation (EU) 2019/933 has applied since 1 July 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dates determine which legal regime applies to SPCs granted in different periods and may affect transitional or country‑specific application (e.g., later application where national law lagged on plant protection product patentability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objective / background of SPCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPC aims to offset the reduction in effective patent protection caused by the time between applying for a patent and receiving authorisation to place a product on the market, to encourage innovation and prevent industries moving away from EU countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contextual purpose informs interpretation of SPC provisions (i.e., balancing incentives for innovation against public interest in competition and access).
